title: Photomorphogenic Regulation of Anthocyanin Biosynthetic Genes via Blue-to-Red Spectral Ratios
description: PhD research quantifying Chalcone Synthase (CHS, EC 2.3.1.74) and Dihydroflavonol 4-Reductase (DFR) gene expression under dynamic LED blue (450nm) to red (660nm) flux ratios.
image_caption: Red and blue LED treatment array inducing vacuolar anthocyanin accumulation in red lettuce leaf epidermis.
overview: Anthocyanins serve as photoprotective antioxidant pigments in plant vacuoles. This doctoral paper demonstrates that modulating the Blue (450nm) to Red (660nm) photon flux ratio (B:R) from 0.15 to 0.45 under a constant DLI (16 mol/m²/day) triggers a 3.8-fold up-regulation of Chalcone Synthase (CHS, EC 2.3.1.74) and Dihydroflavonol 4-Reductase (DFR) transcript levels. The resulting enzymatic cascade increases total cyanidin 3-O-glucoside content by +142%, enhancing UV stress tolerance and postharvest shelf life without penalizing biomass accumulation.
